The halide family is only partly explored (LiF), so this tests a different anion chemistry.

proposals.hypothesis: LiBr is a wide-gap lithium halide that is structurally and chemically close to the chloride coatings. Its halide anion can be partly exchanged with the Cl- in Li6PS5Cl, which may limit the PCl5/SCl4 contact products that dominate the penalty for the chlorides. Its fully reduced halide chemistry should also keep it non-oxidizing at the 4.0 V LiCoO2 contact.
proposals.motivation: Chloride coatings Li2ZnCl4 and Li2MgCl4 gave the lowest penalties so far (0.189 eV, bin 9), but both still formed PCl5/SCl4 at the electrolyte contact. LiMgCl3 failed to build, and the remaining untested halide family members are bromide and fluoride-rich compounds. LiF (0.310 eV) was worse than the chlorides, so bromide is the next most informative halide to test.
